content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passes all quality checks. **This is the first SDD gate — please review before we plan or write any code.**

## 📄 Specification ready for your review

- **Feature directory**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: all items pass ✅ (no open clarifications)

### What the spec proposes — in plain terms

A personal, single-user web app for saving and managing bookmarks, sliced into prioritized user stories:

| Priority | User story | In short |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| **P1** | Save a bookmark | Paste a web address (+ optional title/tags); invalid links are rejected |
| **P1** | Browse & find | See all bookmarks, search by keyword, open links in a new tab |
| **P2** | Organize with tags | Tag bookmarks and filter the list by tag |
| **P2** | Edit & delete | Correct details; delete with a confirmation step |

**The MVP is the two P1 stories** — save + find. Tags and editing come after.

### Scope boundaries I assumed (v1) — please confirm or correct

- **No user accounts / login** — one personal collection, no sign-in or sharing
- **No automatic page-metadata fetching** — no auto-fetched real titles, favicons, or previews (titles are typed or derived from the address)
- **No browser bookmark import/export**
- Delivered as a **browser-based web app**

I also defined measurable success criteria (e.g. find a bookmark among 500 in under 10 seconds, results within 1 second up to 5,000 bookmarks) and edge cases (duplicates, long/invalid addresses, special characters).

---

### Your options at this gate

1. **Approve** as-is → I proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan).
2. **Request changes** → tell me what to add/remove/correct and I'll update the spec (not the code).
3. **Clarify** → if any of the assumptions above are wrong (especially accounts, or wanting auto-fetched titles/import), say so and I'll fold it in.

Would you like to approve, or should I adjust anything first? I'll hold here and won't start planning until you confirm.

I’m not ready to approve this yet. The single-user browser app is right, but several important behaviours are missing or differ from what I want:

- Saving a link should automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image. I should be able to edit the title and description.
- Saving an address that already exists should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, never offer to create a duplicate.
- A bookmark should also support a personal note, including formatted Markdown.
- Search should cover the title, description, note, and address, and be case-insensitive. I also want `#tag` searches, exact quoted phrases, and combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- Existing tags should be suggested while I type.
- I need a read-later state, with a separate unread view and a way to mark items read.
- I need sorting, plus selecting multiple bookmarks for actions such as changing tags, marking read/unread, archiving, or deleting. The same actions should be usable for all results in the current filtered view.
- Archiving must be separate from deletion: archived links should disappear from the normal list and search but remain available in their own view and be restorable.
- I want saved reusable views that combine a search with included or excluded tags.
- I do want browser bookmark import and export, preserving titles, tags, and original dates.
- I want each page preserved as a local snapshot, with PDFs saved as PDFs, plus an option to save it through the Internet Archive.
- Basic display preferences such as default sorting, number of items shown, and font size should be included.

Please revise the specification around those expectations before moving to planning.

## 📐 Implementation plan ready for review

- **Plan**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`
- **Research (decisions)**: `research.md`
- **Data model**: `data-model.md`
- **Contracts**: `contracts/api.md`, `contracts/search-grammar.md`
- **Run/validate guide**: `quickstart.md`

### How I propose to build it — in plain terms

**One self-contained web app.** A Node.js server both runs the API and serves the interface on port 4000, with everything stored locally — no external database or account system to set up. This matches the single-user, runnable-app setup you approved.

| Concern | Approach | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Storage** | Embedded SQLite file + a full-text search index; snapshots/images saved as files on disk | Fast search over thousands of bookmarks; nothing external to install |
| **Auto-collect title/description/favicon/preview** | Fetch each page and read its standard metadata, using the built-in Chromium browser for pages that need it | Covers ~90%+ of typical pages; missing bits fall back gracefully |
| **Local snapshots** | Save a self-contained copy of each page; real PDFs kept as PDFs; runs in the background so saving stays fast | Preserves pages against link-rot without slowing you down |
| **Internet Archive** | Optional per-bookmark save; if it's unreachable it fails quietly and never blocks your save | As you confirmed |
| **Search** | A dedicated query parser implements your rules: fields, case-insensitive, `#tag`, quoted phrases, AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, implicit AND, quoted-operator-as-text | Encodes exactly the search behavior you specified |
| **Interface** | A responsive single-page app (list, unread, archive, detail/edit, saved views, import/export, preferences) | Supports multi-select, tag suggestions, live search, saved views |

### Notable design decisions worth your eye

- **Enrichment & snapshots run in the background** after a save completes, so saving feels instant; per-item status (pending / ready / failed) is shown.
- **Duplicate detection** stores a normalized key (lowercased host, trailing-slash-insensitive) but keeps your original address for opening/display.
- **Import/export** uses the standard browser bookmark HTML format (folders → tags, original dates preserved).
- **Constitution gate**: the project's constitution file is an empty template, so there are no formal gates to check — I've held the plan to general simplicity/testability discipline and recorded that in the plan.

### Two things to confirm (defaults I chose, easy to change)

1. **Frontend stack**: React built with Vite, served as static files by the same server. Happy to go simpler (server-rendered, no React) if you'd prefer fewer moving parts.
2. **Phasing**: The spec is large (13 stories). I suggest tasks build the **P1 slice first** (save + enrich, no-duplicate, browse/sort/open, search) as a working MVP, then P2 (read-later, tags, notes, bulk, archive), then P3 (saved views, import/export, snapshots+Archive, preferences). Say the word if you'd rather sequence differently.

---

## ✅ Two clarifications locked in

**1. Failures are always visibly surfaced (never quiet)**
- **Spec** — FR-041 now: failure MUST be *visibly* surfaced, never a silent no-op, and the *outcome of both operations (success or failure) MUST be visible*. New US12 scenario 5 covers the Internet Archive failure case explicitly.
- **Plan** — Constraints section states it outright; `snapshot_status` / `archive_org_status` carry a `failed` state the UI must show.
- **Contracts / data-model / quickstart** — each `failed` status is documented as surfaced in the UI; the validation scenario checks a visible `failed` state.

**2. Snapshot = self-contained single HTML file (PDF stays PDF)**
- **Spec** — FR-038 now requires a *self-contained single HTML file usable offline without fetching any asset from the original site*; FR-039/US12 keep PDFs as the original PDF. New edge case added.
- **Plan / research** — the snapshot approach spells out: render, then serialize into **one** `.html` with CSS inlined, images/fonts embedded as `data:` URIs, scripts neutralized, no callbacks to the source site; rejected alternatives (remote-asset snapshot, asset folder) noted.
- **Data-model / contracts / quickstart** — `snapshot_kind: html` documented as a single self-contained file; the validation scenario verifies it renders offline with the network blocked.

No `.specify/extensions.yml`, so no post-implement hooks. Implementation is complete and running. Here's the completion report.

## ✅ Implementation complete — Bookmark Manager

All **82 tasks** in `tasks.md` are done and marked `[X]`, validated against the approved spec by **47 passing automated tests**. The app is **running for your review at `http://maker:4000`** (clean, empty state, ready to use).

### What was built
A single-user, self-contained web app (Node.js + Express + embedded SQLite, React/Vite UI, Chromium via Playwright for enrichment/snapshots). One `npm start` serves the API and UI on `0.0.0.0:4000`; all data lives under `data/` — no external services needed.

Every approved user story is implemented and test-covered:

| | Story | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Save + auto-enrich (title/description/favicon/preview), edit all fields | E2E + API |
| P1 | No duplicates → route to existing (trailing-slash/host-case aware) | E2E |
| P1 | Browse, sort, open, empty/no-results states | E2E |
| P1 | Advanced search (fields, case-insensitive, `#tag`, phrases, AND/OR/NOT, parens, implicit AND, quoted-operator-as-text, malformed→error) | 12 unit + E2E |
| P2 | Read-later (not auto-set) + unread view | E2E |
| P2 | Tags + type-ahead suggestions + include/exclude filter | E2E |
| P2 | Markdown notes (rendered + sanitized) | E2E |
| P2 | Bulk & view-wide actions (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete) | E2E |
| P2 | Archive vs delete (restore; **single-delete confirmation**) | E2E |
| P3 | Saved views | E2E |
| P3 | Import/export (Netscape HTML, titles/tags/dates, no dup) | node + E2E |
| P3 | Self-contained single-HTML snapshots (renders offline), PDFs as PDFs, Internet Archive, **all outcomes visibly surfaced** | E2E (offline render + visible-failure checks) |
| P3 | Display preferences (default sort, items, font size) | E2E |

**Test tally:** 21 vitest unit · 4 import/export (node) · 1 **restart-persistence** (spawns→kills→restarts the real process, checks SC-007) · 21 Playwright browser E2E. Search returns in **4–22 ms at 5,000 bookmarks** (target was <1 s).

### Fidelity issues I caught and fixed during implementation
Routed through the spec (no vibe-patching): user-supplied title/description are no longer clobbered by auto-enrichment; searching *within* the archive view now works; the default-sort preference actually drives the list; single-delete confirmation is wired through the shared confirm dialog. I also added US9 acceptance scenario 5 to the spec for single-delete confirmation and T082 for restart persistence.

### Two honest implementation notes
- **Search matching uses SQL `LIKE` (case-insensitive substring)** rather than the FTS5 index the plan mentioned — because your spec requires *substring* matching, which FTS5's token matching wouldn't satisfy. The FTS table exists but the executor uses `LIKE`; performance is well within target.
- A native `better-sqlite3`/Node 24 crash on statement garbage-collection was the root cause of early flakiness; fixed by caching prepared statements (also faster). The DB-backed tests run under Node's test runner (not vitest's worker pool) to avoid the same teardown issue.
- Frontend files are slightly consolidated vs. the task paths (e.g. components in `components.jsx`/`pages.jsx` rather than one file each) — functionally equivalent and complete.

You can review the app now at **`http://maker:4000`** — add a URL and watch it auto-enrich, try the search operators, tags, archive/restore, import/export, and preferences. Let me know what you'd like adjusted; any change will go back through the spec first, per our workflow.

I accept the completed application. The implementation report covers the behavior we approved, including the final confirmation and restart-persistence requirements, and the running app presents the expected views and controls.
